column.text: Bitcoin is currently trading above $78K despite a massive $9.71 billion in liquidations over the last two weeks, signaling that institutional distribution via spot ETFs is successfully offsetting retail accumulation while short-covering dynamics fuel upward momentum. The market bias remains cautiously bullish with a 6 out of 10 confidence score driven by high stablecoin liquidity even as we see $201M in recent ETF outflows. We are witnessing classic short squeeze characteristics where shorts were liquidated at a rate of $6.8 million versus only $1.0 million for longs, creating a choppy but upward-biased environment that ignores traditional tech weakness. The correlation between Bitcoin and the Nasdaq has effectively broken to -0.01, meaning crypto-native momentum dictates price action regardless of semiconductor selling pressure on Nvidia or cooling AI sentiment following their record Q2 revenue report. While Tim Cook steps down as Apple CEO next week and OpenAI expands access to its Astra model, the primary risk remains a potential decoupling if tech hardware stocks face continued headwinds while inflation comments from Kevin Warsh keep rates hawkish. Dollar liquidity is currently flat with no macro tailwind or headwind either way, so traders must focus on price structure rather than waiting for external catalysts. Solana passed its governance proposal to double disinflation and Fogo halted mainnet operations after a hack, yet the broader narrative stays focused on institutional flows and retail chasing highs like the recent Niu Lai token spike. The tape is up-trending with continuation longs carrying the tailwind while shorts need real mechanisms like overheated funding or supply unlocks before entering counter-trend positions.
